given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Loans due 2026-03-16 are checked on 2026-03-17, so overdue is set up. The test clock sets a plain date, and nothing exercises the UTC day boundary.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs against a fresh database with no reminders, so the loans start with none recorded.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: `fakeNotifications.sent` must hold exactly two entries, each with the right memberId, loanId and dueOn. Skipping the call, or sending the wrong member, would fail.
The reminders table must hold exactly the two loan ids.
B1 selects only `loan_id`, never `sent_on`, so recording `dueOn` instead of today would still pass. Only B3's test (line 103-105) pins `sent_on`.
B3 proves a refused reminder is not recorded. mutants.json lists this ordering as not mutated for that reason.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The first run records loan1's reminder, and the second run on the same day is the case where one already exists.
loan2 is overdue and is returned through the app before the job runs.
member-3's loan is due on 2026-03-17, which is today, so it sits exactly on the boundary.

then.why: `toMatchObject` on an array needs the same length, so `sent` must be exactly [loan1]. A resend, a returned loan or the boundary loan would each fail it.

given.why: `refuseFor(loan1, ...)` makes the fake return a refused result.
B5's test shows that a failed connection becomes a refused result. The service test only uses a refusal.
Both loans are overdue and the job runs.

then.why: The reminders table must contain only loan2's row, so a record for loan1 would fail.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`
then.why: The exact entry is matched on level, event, loanId and error text.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan1 is older and refused, and loan2 is still sent.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, one of them refused, and the job runs over all of them.

then.why: The last log entry must equal level info, event `reminders.finished` and fields sent 2, failed 1. The counts differ, so swapping them or dropping one would fail.

given.why: A reminder object is passed straight to the client.

then.part: Sends `POST {NOTIFY_URL}/notifications` with JSON `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The captured request must equal the method, path, content-type and full body exactly.
202, 200 and 204 are each accepted, which rules out a check for 200 only.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 gives kind refused and a reason containing "400".

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error gives kind refused and a reason containing "unreachable".
